data.why: The GUI has no file-upload control (Predict/Train forms only take server-side filesystem paths validated by regex), the repo ships no pretrained ML_models/ classifier as the candidate record claimed, and the README's own training dataset (Edwards et al.) is hosted off GitHub, so a small host/virus genome set with phastDNA's required host.json/virus.json taxonomy metadata was fabricated so the scientist can train a toy classifier and immediately use it for prediction.

goals: Train a phage-host range classifier from labeled bacterial host genomes and their infecting phage genomes
Use a trained (or pretrained) classifier to predict the most likely bacterial host(s) for an unknown virus genome
Compare predicted host rankings against taxonomic ground truth to judge how taxonomically specific the prediction is
Tune fastDNA/embedding hyperparameters (k-mer size, read length, embedding dimension) to see their effect on host-prediction accuracy
Flag ambiguous or low-quality query genomes (mixed k-mer signal, N-gaps) where host prediction confidence is low

review.summary: The training-form setup, prediction launch and job page are mapped well, with clean general/specific wording and mostly accurate evidence (2 of 11 checked screens are miscited). The backend never actually ran in this environment (Train returned 500 on a missing form key, and phastdna.py crashed on a pandas/Modin import), so the core science is missing: launching training, the iteration and score view, model selection, and reading host predictions. It needs a fixed environment and a re-exploration of those stages before filing.
